title: Replication package: Level Breaks and Finite-Sample GLS Detrending
description: Replication code and public data for the paper 'Level Breaks and Finite-Sample GLS Detrending: The Point-Optimal Unit Root Test and the Purchasing Power Parity Puzzle'. A single Numba-compiled numerical kernel (src/mlb/kernel_numba.py) drives all Monte Carlo; the package is numba-only by design (no NumPy fallback ships). A single entry point, replicate.py, reproduces every printed exhibit: it reads the frozen golden outputs by default (--quick) and regenerates from scratch on demand (--full). Five self-contained doors under section_replications/ organize the work: (1) critical_values -- the finite-sample point-optimal calibration, tabulating the P_T statistic and the four M-class statistics (MZ_alpha, MZ_t, MSB, MPT) at the 1/2.5/5/10 percent points by (m, T) at cbar=-7, produced by a K=20 block design of 165,000 replications per block (3,300,000 per cell); (2) robustness -- the AR(1) size/power study; (3) bootstrap_empirical -- the PPP application (sieve and wild bootstrap, median-unbiased half-lives) and the Pesaran cross-sectional-dependence diagnostic (pesaran_cd.py); (4) supplement -- the online-supplement S2 and section 6.3 numerics (empirical modulus, dependence PMF and bound, assumption checks); (5) figures -- figure rendering from the doors' output. All printed tables and figures reproduce from files inside the package.
